channel_delta.evidence: The three added channels cannot be named. Two independent routes were attempted and both failed: the prior document was pinned under storage reference_only, so its bytes were never retained and are no longer fetchable; and the provider's own JSON-RPC changelog, which explicitly covers subscription updates, carries no entry for the 2026-08-18 deploy at all (its most recent entry is Release 21.07.2026). Removal is excluded positively rather than by absence of evidence: every authored channel family was confronted individually against the current channel key set and all are present.

removal_confrontation.method: each authored WebSocket channel family resolved against the current channel key set by exact name or dotted prefix

upcoming_surface_comparison.evidence: The current and upcoming channel key sets hash identically and their set difference is empty in both directions, so the current WebSocket surface has caught up to the already-reviewed upcoming inventory. The documents still differ by 526 bytes with an identical channel and operation inventory, so the residual difference is descriptive text rather than contract shape; the two documents are not interchangeable and the upcoming artifact keeps its own pin.

pin_key_decision.reason: The provider rewrote the current document twice on 2026-08-18 while info.version remained 1.0.0, matching the REST surface, so the declared version cannot identify the reviewed bytes.

etag_disqualified_as_pin_key.observation: On this same refetch both upcoming artifacts served byte-identical documents under new ETags: upcoming-openapi kept sha256 788ae5db... and 1438672 bytes while its ETag moved from W/"5e8b26e0df446ae0b6b213d91184f49b" to W/"QCggKABm3LEi7g4f", and upcoming-asyncapi kept sha256 8fb075b8... and 609774 bytes while its ETag moved from W/"2863755d34671127f41d92e5de11f775" to W/"BC1C2b7GgspzdS5u".
etag_disqualified_as_pin_key.consequence: The ETag changed for documents whose content did not, and the ETag format itself changed from a 32-character hexadecimal form to a 16-character opaque form, which indicates a provider-side serving change rather than a contract change. An ETag-keyed gate would therefore have raised two false drift alarms on this refetch. The ETag remains recorded as descriptive provenance and is not the integrity key.
etag_disqualified_as_pin_key.gate_behaviour_confirmed: mix bourse.authority_check --online exited 0 with all four Deribit specification artifacts reported as upstream unchanged, confirming the gate compares sha256 and not the ETag half of the composite pin.

continuity.relation: The same maintenance deploy republished both documents, evidenced by an identical ETag W/"DXTaA468CADkchO3" and an identical Last-Modified of Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:26:03 GMT on the current REST and current WebSocket artifacts.

limitations: storage reference_only means drift on this artifact is detectable but never diffable: a hash mismatch proves the document changed and cannot show what changed.
The added channels are counted but unnamed, so this report establishes that the authored surface survived the change and does not establish what the provider gained.
decision_reason: The republished document is the shipped current WebSocket surface: it matches the already-reviewed upcoming 43-channel inventory exactly, adds channels without removing any authored family's upstream definition, and leaves every authored dispatch and subscription target reachable.
